action: General advice: inventory certificates chaining to eMudhra roots and replace them with certificates from another CA, and apply current Windows and macOS updates.
exec: iTnews reports that Microsoft and Apple are ending trust in eMudhra roots, so sites using its certificates need certificates from another authority.
impact: Certificates under the affected hierarchies stop being trusted on major platforms; issuance from the older G1 hierarchy stopped on November 17.
plain: iTnews reports that an Indian company that issues website security certificates had a script bug that cut some private keys to a single byte. Microsoft and Apple are removing trust in its certificates.
summary: iTnews reports the Indian certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight more intermediate CAs; its incident report says a single line in a homebrew Python script truncated ECDSA private values to their leading byte. iTnews says Microsoft will remove all 10 remaining eMudhra roots from 16 November, and eMudhra said Apple would end trust on 30 November. iTnews also says eMudhra is leaving public TLS and has withdrawn its RSA assurance.
title: eMudhra revokes eight more CAs as Microsoft pulls trust in all its roots
date_note: Date is iTnews's report (13 Nov) of Microsoft's root removal; BleepingComputer (11 Nov) says eMudhra revoked the eight further RSA intermediates on 7 November.

validation.note: Two independent publishers (iTnews, BleepingComputer) state the core facts: eight more intermediate CAs revoked, a script bug that reduced ECDSA private keys to a single byte, and eMudhra's exit from public TLS. Microsoft removing all 10 remaining roots from 16 November and Apple ending trust on 30 November are stated by iTnews only; BleepingComputer gives 16 November as the date eMudhra stops issuing under G1 and says the RSA keys were not weakened but eMudhra could not show it handled them under its policies.

review.note: who said it / stronger than source: summary now attributes to iTnews and eMudhra's incident report; dropped unsupported October compromise, plain 'anyone could guess' and 'curl and git'; exec and action reworded.
